primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.primary: Owned complete RU The Body Keeps the Score, Ivan Chorny translation, Eksmo edition
primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.locator: content.opf; content0.html and full spine; five parts, twenty chapters and epilogue/end matter
primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.actuallyChecked: Metadata/spine and substantial primary chapter material establish a full work, not a third-party condensation. Access read-only.

primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.locator: content1.html Tom opening and medication refusal; content3.html numbness/court; content4.html veterans; content10.html pool/pharmacology; content11–12.html Marsha/scanning
primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.actuallyChecked: Refusal motive is Tom’s explicit explanation. Pool/laboratory and continued limited medication benefit are in the author’s account. Marsha’s reminder is an actual described study.

primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.locator: content13–19.html threat appraisal and Stan/Ute (especially content17–18); content20.html relational/polyvagal explanation; content24–29.html self-perception/alexithymia; content32–37.html attachment and Marilyn
primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.actuallyChecked: Contrasting reliving/shutdown, responsiveness, internal sensation/agency, attachment contradiction and Marilyn’s operating-room-nurse/tennis/intimacy account; no invented trauma scene found.

primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.locator: content43–44.html Felitti/ACE; content46–50.html developmental-trauma proposal; content52.html ordinary versus traumatic memory; content57.html delayed return claims; content50–59.html Janet/memory discussion
primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.actuallyChecked: Protective meaning of regained weight; proposal status of developmental trauma; author’s strong persistence/recovery claims remain attributed. Primary targeted passages, not independent verification of patient histories.

primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.locator: content60.html recovery/agency; content65–69.html treatment/language position; content71.html writing; content75–79.html EMDR, especially complete represented trial discussion in content76; content81 and content83.html Annie/yoga; content86–87.html Joan; content89–93.html structures/neurofeedback
primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.actuallyChecked: Actual method reasoning; EMDR comparison and adult/childhood distinction; Annie’s difficult first class and subsequent reporting; Joan’s destabilization in IFS terms; present symbolic support and measured feedback.

primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.locator: content99–104.html theatre and epilogue, particularly content101.html Urban Improv, content102.html Possibility Project, content103.html Shakespeare in the Courts, content104.html collective prevention
primaryEvidenceActuallyChecked.actuallyChecked: Different programmes remain different: interrupted choice scene, original musical, existing Shakespeare roles. Public prevention framing is the author’s own.
Current adult PTSD overview identifies PE/CPT/EMDR as strongest-supported trauma-focused therapies and unequal support for other methods.
Grossman abstract only: explicit challenge to physiological/evolutionary premises; no full-literature appraisal claimed.
Otgaar review sections on repression controversy, suggestion and false autobiographical memory; supports the narrow qualification, not denial of survivors’ reports.

contentJudgment: The five-part author argument remains coherent, with actual clinical/institutional examples and a return to agency and collective prevention. Author interpretation, contemporary criticism and present clinical guidance remain distinguishable. No material invention, reversal, lost essential qualification or bilingual meaning error found.

wording.ru: «В книге обсуждаются различия результатов, в том числе по истории травмы».
wording.en: “The book discusses differing results, including by trauma history.”

optionalSuggestions.readerEffect: This reports that results exist without giving their direction. The integration argument is already conveyed in emdr-experience, so this does not invalidate the condensation.
optionalSuggestions.minimalSuggestion: Optionally replace the generic result sentence with one attributed sentence: in the author’s comparison EMDR improvements proved more durable after treatment, with better results for adult-onset than childhood trauma. Retain author-led status and do not infer an individual treatment choice. No statistics or additional screen needed.
optionalSuggestions.sourceLocator: Chapter 15, content76.html, «Изучение ДПДГ», follow-up and adult-versus-childhood paragraphs.

materialLimitations: Targeted primary argument/case checking across the represented book, not continuous full-edition reading or all-notes verification.
No independently verified patient records; these remain the author’s accounts. English translation was compared with the represented primary meaning, not with a complete English edition.
Current sources were checked for the narrow qualifications used, not a systematic clinical review or approval of any treatment for an individual.
Verdict covers the hashed revised collector package. Root HTML still contained 144 old pairs at inspection. Publication/root integration and browser/device QA remain publisher-owned.
